Q: How can I stop relying on AI when writing code? A:

Do you know the basic grammar?
for example
int x = 5;
do you understand every part?

For more complex lines, see if you can understand what each part is doing.

Some languages use a lot of shortcuts. Which language are you working with?

Q: What are the important notions in C that you did not learn from your teachers? A:

My teachers spent so much time teaching us that pointers are scary little goobers that can cause lots of problems if not used correctly, that they never bothered to show us how powerful they can really be.

For example, the concept of pointer arithmetic was foreign to me until I had already been using C++ for several years:

Examples:

  • c[0] is equivalent to *c
  • c[1] is equivalent to *(c + 1)
  • Loop iteration: for(char* c = str; *c != '\0'; c++)
  • and so on...

Rather than making students afraid to use pointers, teach them how to use them appropriately.

As brought to my attention by a comment, I just read on a different answer, I think there is also some value in discussing the subtle differences between pointers and arrays (and how to put the two together to facilitate some pretty complex structures), as well as how to properly use the const keyword with respect to pointer declarations.

Q: How to Move the mouse using VBScript A:

It's not really possible to move the cursor using VBScript. However, you can determine the current cursor position by using the MSHTML event object and its screenX and screenY properties, like this:

Dim objDocument, objEvent

Set objDocument = CreateObject("htmlfile")
Set objEvent = objDocument.createEventObject()
MsgBox "Current cursor position: " &_
   "X = " & objEvent.screenX &_
   ", Y = " & objEvent.screenY
